board_authority: Board of Secondary Education, Andhra Pradesh (Directorate of Government Examinations)
ownership: Government and Government-aided (many private schools also follow the State syllabus)
classes_covered: Classes 1-10 (Class 10 is the SSC board-exam year)
medium_of_instruction: Set per school (medium is recorded for each candidate in the SSC nominal roll)
key_exam: SSC Public Examination (Class 10); Advanced Supplementary Examination (ASE) in May for those who fail
exam_window: SSC March 2026 was held 16-03-2026 to 01-04-2026 (9:30 AM - 12:45 PM; science papers 9:30-11:30 AM); ASE May 2026 results are out. SSC 2027 blueprint and model papers were released 12-07-2026; the 2027 time table is not yet out
passing_criteria: Each subject is examined for 100 marks with no weightage for internal marks (G.O.Ms.No.41, 2019): First language, Second language, English, Mathematics, Social Studies, and General Science as two papers (Physical Science and Biological Science, 50 marks each on separate days). The pass mark is not yet confirmed from a BSEAP document
next_step: Intermediate (BIE AP), AP POLYCET diploma, ITI, or APOSS / NIOS open schooling
approx_fee: Free in government schools; SSC exam fee as notified by BSEAP each year
source: BSEAP (bse.ap.gov.in): SSC Public Examinations March 2026 revised time table dated 04-02-2026, Head Masters' instructions Rc.No.HMI/1/SSC-2025-DGE dated 02-12-2025, press note Rc.No.01/DCGE-1/Confd/SSC March 2027 dated 12-07-2026

board_authority: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)
ownership: Private (a smaller number are Central Govt schools like KVs/JNVs)
medium_of_instruction: English (most common); some Hindi/Telugu medium sections
key_exam: CBSE Class 10 Board Examination
exam_window: February-March (results typically by May)
passing_criteria: Pass mark 33% per subject
next_step: Same downstream choices as SSC students: Intermediate/Junior College (can continue CBSE Class 11-12 or move to AP Intermediate board), POLYCET diploma, or ITI
approx_fee: Varies widely by school (typically Rs 20,000 - Rs 2,00,000+/year) - unverified, needs school-by-school follow-up
source: AP Intermediate admission eligibility notes (brinto.in)

board_authority: Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE)
classes_covered: Classes 1-10 (10 is the board-exam year, called ICSE)
medium_of_instruction: English
key_exam: ICSE (Class 10) Examination
exam_window: February-March
passing_criteria: Minimum ~33-35 marks out of 100 per subject to pass (theory + internal/practical)
next_step: Same downstream options as CBSE/SSC students; ICSE is explicitly recognised as an equivalent qualifying board for AP Intermediate admission
approx_fee: Typically among the higher-fee private school options - exact figures vary per school, unverified
source: collegedekho.com ICSE passing marks guide; brinto.in AP Intermediate admission guide

board_authority: Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Education, Government of India; CBSE-affiliated
medium_of_instruction: Mother tongue or regional language up to Class 8, then English for Mathematics and Science and Hindi for Social Science. The JNVST can be written in Hindi, English, Telugu, Marathi, Urdu, Oriya or Kannada
key_exam: JNVST (Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Selection Test) for Class 6; CBSE board exams in Classes 10 and 12
exam_window: JNVST 2027 (for 2027-28): last date to apply was 31-07-2026; the test is on 28-11-2026 and admit cards are out at cbseitms.rcil.gov.in/nvs
passing_criteria: Merit in the JNVST. Born between 01-05-2015 and 31-07-2017; bona fide resident of the district and studying Class 5 there in 2026-27 (or in a neighbouring district within 10 km of home, still applying to the home district's JNV). At least 75% of seats go to rural candidates; SC/ST seats in proportion to district population (at least 15% / 7.5%), 27% OBC (central list), at least one-third girls. Up to 80 students per JNV
next_step: Students continue at the JNV through Class 12 under CBSE. Andhra Pradesh has 15 JNVs (13 plus 2 sanctioned for SC/ST-concentrated districts)
approx_fee: Education, board, lodging, uniforms and textbooks are free. Classes 9-12 pay Vidyalaya Vikas Nidhi of Rs.600 a month (wards of Government employees up to Rs.1,500 or the Children Education Allowance); SC/ST, Divyang, all girls and BPL families are exempt
source: NVS JNVST 2027 Prospectus (cbseitms.rcil.gov.in/nvs/assets/pdf/Final_Prospectus_2027.pdf: section 1.1 state-wise JNVs, eligibility clause 4, reservation of seats, medium-of-test table) and the JNVST portal announcement (admit cards live)

board_authority: Sainik Schools Society, Ministry of Defence, Government of India; CBSE-affiliated
medium_of_instruction: English
key_exam: AISSEE (All India Sainik Schools Entrance Examination), conducted by NTA
exam_window: AISSEE-2026 is complete (results declared, online counselling running). The AISSEE-2027 information bulletin is not yet out; watch sainikschoolsociety.in and exams.nta.nic.in/sainik-school-society
passing_criteria: Admission at Class 6 and Class 9 on AISSEE performance; eligibility, exam scheme and reservation are set in each year's Information Bulletin
next_step: Andhra Pradesh has two Sainik Schools: Sainik School Korukonda and Sainik School Kalikiri. Students continue to Class 12 with preparation for NDA
approx_fee: Set by each school (Korukonda collects the 2026-27 school fee online on sainikschoolkorukonda.org); amount not yet checked
source: Sainik Schools Society website (sainikschoolsociety.in: home page and 'Existing Schools' list) and Sainik School Korukonda website (sainikschoolkorukonda.org), read 2026-10-31

school_type: Rashtriya Military School (RMS) - none located in AP
board_authority: Rashtriya Military Schools, Ministry of Defence, Government of India; CBSE-affiliated
medium_of_instruction: English
key_exam: RMS Common Entrance Test (OMR based) for Class 6 and Class 9, held in December
exam_window: Last date and test date are set in each year's CET notification on rashtriyamilitaryschools.edu.in
passing_criteria: Age 10-12 years for Class 6 and 13-15 years for Class 9 on 31 March of the admission year; admission against available vacancies. The site's admission page says admissions are for boys only, but its latest notice invites boys and girls - check the current CET notification
next_step: There is no RMS in Andhra Pradesh: the five campuses are at Ajmer and Dholpur (Rajasthan), Bengaluru and Belgaum (Karnataka) and Chail (Himachal Pradesh), open to students from any state through the CET
approx_fee: Not yet checked against a primary document
source: Rashtriya Military Schools official website (rashtriyamilitaryschools.edu.in: 'Our Schools' and 'Admission' pages, and the latest-news item 'Applications for admission to Class VI and IX for boys and girls'), read 2026-10-31

school_type: AP Gurukulam Residential Schools (APSWREIS / APTWREIS / APMJPBCWREIS / APREIS)
board_authority: Respective AP Welfare Societies - Social/Tribal/BC Welfare / General Residential Educational Institutions Societies, Govt of Andhra Pradesh
ownership: Government (State Govt, residential, largely free for eligible community students)
classes_covered: Classes 5-12 (main entry at Class 5 via joint APGPCET; lateral entry at Classes 6-9 via society-specific CETs)
medium_of_instruction: Predominantly English medium
key_exam: APGPCET (joint 5th-class entrance test) or society-specific tests: APSWRS CET (SC), APTWRS CET (ST), APBCWRS CET (BC), APRS CET (general/open)
exam_window: Confirmed via the 2026 cycle: notification last week of Jan 2026, online applications through 31 Mar 2026, entrance exam 24 Apr 2026 - so the window runs Jan-Apr rather than Feb-Apr. Covers 185 Balayogi (SW) + 31 Tribal Welfare + 61 MJP BC Welfare residential schools (277 schools total). That cycle is closed; 2027 cycle notification not yet out as of this data pull (Sept 2026)
passing_criteria: Community-specific eligibility (SC/ST/BC/general); admission by merit rank in the relevant CET
next_step: Continues within the same society to Class 11-12 via RJC CET, then optionally RDC CET for degree-level admission inside the Gurukulam system, or external entrance exams after Class 12
approx_fee: Free or heavily subsidised for eligible community students
source: teachernews.in / teachersbadi.in / jnanabhumiap.in APGPCET 2026 notification pages (verified Sept 2026)

board_authority: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Govt of India, implemented in AP via APTWREIS (Gurukulam) - CBSE affiliated
ownership: Government (Central Govt scheme, residential, ST students only)
classes_covered: Classes 6-12 (main entry at Class 6; Class 7/8 entry only against backlog vacancies)
medium_of_instruction: English (CBSE English medium)
key_exam: AP EMRS CET
exam_window: Confirmed via the 2026-27 cycle: notification released ~Jan 2026, consistent with the Jan-Mar window. Covers 28 EMRS schools across AP, 1,680 Class-6 seats (840 boys/840 girls); selection via the EMRSST (2-hour test, no negative marking, Telugu/English medium)
passing_criteria: Open only to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students, priority to PVTG students in remote areas; merit rank in the CET
next_step: Continues to Class 12 within the EMRS (CBSE board), then the same downstream entrance-exam pathways as other CBSE students
approx_fee: Free (fully funded Central Govt scheme for ST students)
source: apteachers.in / teachersbadi.in AP EMRS 2026-27 admissions notification (verified Sept 2026)

school_type: NIOS (National Institute of Open Schooling) - Secondary Course
board_authority: National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS), Ministry of Education, Government of India; Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are served by NIOS Regional Centre Hyderabad (rchyderabad.nios.ac.in)
ownership: Government (Central, autonomous); taught through NIOS Accredited Institutions (study centres)
medium_of_instruction: Secondary can be taken in Hindi, English, Urdu, Marathi, Telugu, Gujarati, Malayalam, Tamil, Odia, Punjabi, Assamese, Sanskrit or Kannada medium
key_exam: NIOS Secondary public exam, twice a year (March-April and September-October)
exam_window: 2026-27 admission: Block 1 - 16-03-2026 to 31-07-2026 without late fee, late-fee windows to 15-09-2026 (first exam March-April 2027). Block 2 - 16-09-2026 to 31-01-2027 without late fee, late-fee windows to 15-03-2027 (first exam September-October 2027) - Block 2 is open now
passing_criteria: Entry: at least 14 years old (on 31-07-2026 for Block 1, 31-01-2027 for Block 2) with a Class 8 marksheet or self-certificate; no upper age limit. To pass, clear at least five subjects (one or two languages plus others) with 33% aggregate (theory plus practical / internal) in each. Admission is valid for five years
next_step: NIOS Senior Secondary, or Intermediate / POLYCET / ITI like any Class 10 pass
approx_fee: Admission fee for 5 subjects: Rs.2,340 (male), Rs.1,890 (female / third gender), Rs.1,560 (SC/ST, ex-servicemen, PwD); exam fees are extra
source: NIOS Academic Prospectus 2026-27 (sdmis.nios.ac.in > Prospectus 2026-27: medium of instruction, scheme of studies, admission blocks, Table 3 entry requirements, Table 4 fees, Regional Centres list - RC Hyderabad covers Telangana and Andhra Pradesh)

medium_of_instruction: Telugu / English (dual-medium in most govt schools)

school_type: RTE Act - 25% quota in private/unaided schools
board_authority: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act 2009, implemented by AP School Education Dept
classes_covered: Entry class only (typically Class 1, per state rules)
medium_of_instruction: As per the admitted private school's medium of instruction
key_exam: Online application during the state's annual RTE admission notification window; lottery/random selection among eligible applicants when seats are oversubscribed
passing_criteria: Eligibility: Economically Weaker Section (EWS) / disadvantaged-group children as per AP's RTE rules; age as per entry-class norms
next_step: Student continues at the same private school on regular (non-quota) terms in subsequent classes, per RTE continuity provisions
approx_fee: Free - private school waives fees for the reserved 25% seats; school is reimbursed by government per RTE norms
source: amaravathiteacher.com/rte-admission-2025-26-andhra-pradesh-notification; education.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/education/policies-and-schemes/right-to-education/rte-admission (via AP Career Database - 2026-09-21 Drive snapshot, last verified 2026-09-21)

board_authority: Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), Ministry of Education, Government of India; CBSE-affiliated. Regional Office Hyderabad lists 85 KVs
classes_covered: Balvatika (pre-primary, in selected KVs) and Classes 1-12
medium_of_instruction: Not yet checked against a primary KVS document
key_exam: CBSE board exams in Classes 10 and 12; no entrance test for Balvatika or Class 1
exam_window: 2026-27 admissions (closed): online registration for Balvatika-1 & 3 and Class 1 from 20-03-2026 to 02-04-2026; provisional lists 08/09-04-2026, 16-04-2026 and 21-04-2026; offline registration for Balvatika-2 and Class 2 onwards (except 11) 02-04-2026 to 08-04-2026, subject to vacancies. 2027-28 schedule not yet announced
passing_criteria: Class 1 / Balvatika seats are filled from the online lists in this order: RTE seats, Service Priority Categories I and II, then any shortfall in the SC/ST/OBC (NCL) quotas, with an offline notification if online applications fall short
next_step: CBSE board exams in Classes 10 and 12, then the same routes as other CBSE students
approx_fee: Not yet checked against the current KVS fee order
source: KVS Proposed Schedule for Admission 2026-27 (cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3kv01edb5f385049e35efd27c9a97d11f/uploads/2026/03/2026032313.pdf) and KVS Regional Office Hyderabad website (rohyderabad.kvs.gov.in: 85 KVs, 71,521 students, read 2026-10-31)

board_authority: Board of Secondary Education, Telangana (BSE Telangana / TSBSE)
ownership: Government (also followed by many private/aided schools)
medium_of_instruction: Telugu, English, Urdu, Hindi, Marathi (school-dependent)
key_exam: SSC Public Examination (Class 10 Board Exam)
exam_window: 2026: exams held March 14 - April 16, 2026 (morning shift 9:30am-12:30pm); result announced by the Board (per BSE Telangana notification, 2026 result declared in the April-June window)
passing_criteria: Minimum 35% marks required in each subject out of 100
next_step: Choose one: Intermediate (MPC/BiPC/CEC/MEC/HEC), TS POLYCET for a polytechnic diploma, ITI for a trade certificate, or NIOS if unable to continue formal school
approx_fee: Free/nominal in government schools; govt-aided schools may charge small fees - exact figures unverified, needs follow-up
source: bse.telangana.gov.in; shiksha.com/boards/bse-telangana-ssc-board (TS SSC 2026 exam schedule, pass criteria)

passing_criteria: Pass mark 33% per subject (CISCE norm)

board_authority: Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Education, Government of India; CBSE-affiliated
medium_of_instruction: Mother tongue or regional language up to Class 8, then English for Mathematics and Science and Hindi for Social Science. The JNVST can be written in Hindi, English, Telugu, Kannada, Marathi or Urdu
key_exam: JNVST (Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Selection Test) for Class 6; CBSE board exams in Classes 10 and 12
exam_window: JNVST 2027 (for 2027-28): last date to apply was 31-07-2026; the test is on 28-11-2026 and admit cards are out at cbseitms.rcil.gov.in/nvs
passing_criteria: Merit in the JNVST. Born between 01-05-2015 and 31-07-2017; bona fide resident of the district and studying Class 5 there in 2026-27 (or in a neighbouring district within 10 km of home, still applying to the home district's JNV). At least 75% of seats go to rural candidates; SC/ST seats in proportion to district population (at least 15% / 7.5%), 27% OBC (central list), at least one-third girls. Up to 80 students per JNV

school_type: Sainik School - none located in Telangana
board_authority: Sainik Schools Society, Ministry of Defence, Government of India
ownership: Government (Central), residential - none of the Society's existing schools is in Telangana
classes_covered: Classes 6-12 at Sainik Schools in other states
medium_of_instruction: English
key_exam: AISSEE (All India Sainik Schools Entrance Examination), conducted by NTA, for Class 6 and Class 9
exam_window: AISSEE-2027 information bulletin not yet out; watch sainikschoolsociety.in
passing_criteria: Admission on AISSEE performance as per each year's Information Bulletin
next_step: Telangana students can apply through AISSEE to Sainik Schools elsewhere, e.g. Korukonda or Kalikiri in Andhra Pradesh. The Society also affiliates new partnership Sainik Schools; their state-wise list was not checked. (The TGSWREIS 'Sainik schools' at Rukmapur and Jagathgirigutta are Telangana welfare-society schools, entered through TGCET, not Sainik Schools Society schools)
approx_fee: Set by each school
source: Sainik Schools Society website (sainikschoolsociety.in: 'Existing Schools' and 'New Schools' pages), read 2026-10-31

school_type: Telangana Gurukulam Residential Schools (TSWREIS / TTWREIS / MJPTBCWREIS / TREIS)
board_authority: Four Telangana welfare residential societies: TGSWREIS (Social Welfare), TGTWREIS (Tribal Welfare), MJPTBCWREIS (BC Welfare) and TREIS (general)
classes_covered: Entry at Class 5 in all four societies; backlog / regular seats in Classes 6-9 in TGSWREIS, TGTWREIS and MJPTBCWREIS (including the TGSWREIS Sainik schools at Rukmapur and Jagathgirigutta and a fine arts school)
medium_of_instruction: Not yet checked against a primary document
key_exam: TGCET (Telangana Government Common Entrance Test): 2 hours, 100 objective questions, no negative marks (Class 5: Telugu 20, English 25, Maths 25, EVS 20, Mental Ability 10)
exam_window: TGCET 2026 (for 2026-27, closed): online applications until 21-01-2026 (fee Rs.100), test on 22-02-2026, 11 AM - 1 PM. 2027 notification not yet out; watch tgcet.cgg.gov.in
passing_criteria: Must have studied Class 4 (for Class 5 entry) for the full 2025-26 year in the same erstwhile district; admission is district-specific, on merit and reservation. Parents' income below Rs.1,50,000 a year (rural) or Rs.2,00,000 (urban). Class 5 age: born 01-09-2013 to 31-08-2017 for SC/ST, 01-09-2015 to 31-08-2017 for BC / minority / others. Up to 80 students per school in Class 5
next_step: Continue in the society's schools to Class 10 and its junior colleges for Intermediate
approx_fee: Free education with boarding and lodging; TREIS students get food, books and cosmetic charges, while the other three societies also provide uniforms, kit and stationery
source: TGCET-2026 Prospectus for admission to residential educational institutions 2026-27 (tgcet.cgg.gov.in > Prospectus - TGCMNCET2026)

source: tsemrs.telangana.gov.in (23 EMRS schools functioning in Telangana under TSES); nests.tribal.gov.in; testbook.com/emrs-recruitment/emrs-school-list-in-telangana

next_step: Karnataka has a distinctive extra state-level step not seen in AP/Telangana's CBSE rows: before a school may seek CBSE affiliation, it must first obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Department of Public Instruction under the Karnataka Educational Institutions (Issue of No Objection Certificate and Control) Rules, 2022, and separately register/get recognition under the Karnataka Education Act before starting classes. Sources conflict on whether this state NOC is still mandatory for every CBSE applicant: a 2024 Karnataka High Court order describes the NOC as a prerequisite that CBSE itself re-imposed after once dropping it, while an unverified commercial-consultancy source claims a CBSE notification dated 20-Feb-2025 now allows affiliation with or without the state NOC from the 2026-27 session - this claim could not be confirmed against an official CBSE source. Separately, a Karnataka-specific 2024-25 rule requires ALL CBSE and ICSE private schools to teach Kannada as a first or second language, with fines of up to Rs. 25,000 for non-compliance. A 2025 process change moved the state NOC-issuing authority to jurisdictional Deputy Directors of Public Instruction, cutting administrative levels from 8 to 5 and processing time from 35 to 25 days.
